# Presets

Pre-packaged player configurations that bundle state management, skins, and media components for specific use cases.

A **preset** packages what you need for a specific player use case. It can include special [state management](./features.md), one or more [skins](./skins.md) for UI, and specific media components. Instead of assembling these pieces individually, you pick a preset that matches what you’re building.

For example, the `@videojs/react/background` preset includes a media component with autoplay, mute, and loop built in, a skin with no controls, and just the features needed to power them:

**App.tsx**

```tsx
import { BackgroundVideo, BackgroundVideoPlayer, BackgroundVideoSkin } from '@videojs/react/background';
import '@videojs/react/background/skin.css';

function Hero() {
  return (
    <BackgroundVideoPlayer>
      <BackgroundVideoSkin>
        <BackgroundVideo src="hero.mp4" />
      </BackgroundVideoSkin>
    </BackgroundVideoPlayer>
  );
}
```

## Available presets

The default presets are `/video` and `/audio`. These cover the baseline controls you’d expect from the HTML `<video>` and `<audio>` tags. Beyond the defaults, presets target more specific use cases — the `/background` preset, for example, needs layout but not controls. Over time we’ll add more: short-form players, podcast players, TV streaming players, and others.

The video, audio, live video, and live audio presets each export four skins: Default, Neutral, Compat, and Scaffold. For example, React exports `ScaffoldVideoSkin` with `@videojs/react/video/scaffold-skin.css`; HTML registers `<video-scaffold-skin>` through `@videojs/html/video/scaffold-skin`. See [Choose a skin](./skins.md#choose-a-skin) to compare them.

## What’s in a preset

Each React preset exports a named, preconfigured player component and typed `usePlayer` hook, plus the building blocks needed to extend its features, add its skin source to your project, or swap its media component:

- **Player** — A player component named for the preset, such as `VideoPlayer`, already configured with the preset’s feature bundle.
- **Typed hook** — A `usePlayer` hook whose state and actions match the preset.
- **Feature bundle** — An array of [features](./features.md) that define the player’s state and actions. For example, the video feature bundle includes playback, volume, time, fullscreen, and more.
- **Skins** — Pre-built UIs designed for that feature bundle. For example, a video skin renders fullscreen and PiP controls because the video feature bundle includes those features. An audio skin doesn’t.
- **Media component** — One suited to the use case. For example, the background video element bakes in autoplay, mute, and loop.

These parts aren’t equally tied together. Skins depend tightly on their feature bundle — a skin expects specific features to exist. Media components are more interchangeable — you can swap in an HLS or DASH provider without changing your skin or features.

## Customizing a preset

You can customize a preset in three ways: extend its feature bundle, add its skin source to your project, or swap its media component.

### Extend the feature bundle

Add features to a preset’s feature bundle to enable new functionality. For example, adding playback controls to a background video:

**App.tsx**

```tsx
import { Container, createPlayer, playbackFeature, PlayButton } from '@videojs/react';
import { backgroundFeatures, BackgroundVideo } from '@videojs/react/background';

const { Player } = createPlayer({
  features: [...backgroundFeatures, playbackFeature],
});

function Hero() {
  return (
    <Player>
      <Container>
        <BackgroundVideo src="hero.mp4" />
        <PlayButton />
      </Container>
    </Player>
  );
}
```

### Skin source

If a preset’s skin is close but not quite right, [add its source to your project](./customize-skins.md#style-skin-source) and customize its components and styles.

### Swap the media component

A preset’s default media component is just the starting point. You can replace it with any compatible media provider. For example, using an HLS source with the video preset:

```tsx
<VideoPlayer>
  <VideoSkin>
    <HlsJsVideo src="https://example.com/stream.m3u8" />
  </VideoSkin>
</VideoPlayer>
```
